m:duomo: 2026 prices from updated guides (to be confirmed on duomomilano.it): Culture Pass €15 (cathedral, museum, archaeological area, valid 72 hours), with the rooftops on foot €22 or by lift €26; rooftops only €16 on foot or €18 by lift (you always walk down). Cathedral open roughly 8am–6pm, rooftops 9am–7pm with last entry around 6:10pm. Shoulders and knees covered; in rain, ice or strong wind the rooftops may close. The Duomo Museum is closed on Wednesdays.
m:galleria: Free and always open. The cafés and restaurants in the Galleria are the most expensive in the centre: for a coffee or a sandwich it's better to leave the Galleria and look in a side street.
m:scala: Ticket €12 (according to the museum, valid until 31 December 2026). Open every day 9:30am–5:30pm, last entry 5pm. Closed on 7 December, 25 and 26 December, 1 January, Easter, 1 May and 15 August. You can only see the auditorium when there are no rehearsals or performances: the view depends on the day.
m:novecento: Full ticket €10 (civic museums fare in force from 10 May 2026). Hours from guides, to be confirmed: 10am–7:30pm, Thursdays until 10:30pm, closed on Mondays. Free entry on the first Sunday of the month.
m:quadrilatero: Free to stroll around. Shops usually open from 10am to 7–7:30pm; many stay closed on Sunday mornings.
m:castello: Courtyards and Piazza d'Armi free from 7am to 7:30pm. The museums are open Tuesday to Sunday 10am–5:30pm (last entry 4:30pm), closed on Mondays, 25 December, 1 January and 1 May. From 10 May 2026 the museums ticket costs €10 (including the Rondanini Pietà); free entry on the first Sunday of the month. In May 2026 the Sala delle Asse and the prehistory section were closed: check milanocastello.it. The park is open roughly 6:30am–9pm (from guides).
m:cenacolo: Ticket €15 (reduced €2 for ages 18 to 25, free under 18) and booking is compulsory on cenacolovinciano.org: collect your ticket at least 30 minutes before. Sales open in blocks of months and every Wednesday at noon the following week's places are released. Open Tuesday to Sunday 8:15am–7pm (last entry 6:45pm), closed on Mondays, 1 January and 25 December.
m:brera: Free to stroll around. According to guides, the Brera flea market is on the third Sunday of the month, about 9am–7pm, and dates can change in bad weather. The Brera Botanical Garden is a hidden garden behind the Pinacoteca (hours to be checked).
m:pinacoteca: «La Grande Brera» ticket (Pinacoteca and Palazzo Citterio) €20, according to Brera's listing; the Pinacoteca alone cost about €15 in 2025 guides: check on brera.beniculturali.it. Open Tuesday to Sunday 8:30am–7:15pm, last entry 6pm, closed on Mondays, 1 January, 1 May and 25 December. The first Sunday of the month is free with booking.
m:santambrogio: Entry to the basilica is free. Visiting hours vary and should be checked before setting off: according to guides, Monday to Saturday 10am–noon and 2:30–6pm, Sunday afternoon 3–5pm, with visits suspended during services. The new «Ambrosius» museum has a separate ticket (price not read). 7 December is the patron saint's feast day.
m:colonne: Free to see at any time. The basilica has its own hours (to be checked). From here Corso di Porta Ticinese takes you to the Navigli in ten minutes.
m:navigli: Free to stroll at any time. By day it's quiet; from about 6:30pm the bars fill the banks and a drink usually costs more with the snacks included: check the price list before sitting down. On the last Sunday of the month, according to guides, there's the Mercatone dell'Antiquariato antiques market along the Naviglio Grande.
m:portanuova: All free and always accessible. The Bosco Verticale is an apartment block: admire it from outside, from the Biblioteca degli Alberi park. In December there's usually a market on the square.
vd:luini: Since 1949 a short walk from the Duomo: the panzerotto, soft dough folded and fried with a hot tomato and mozzarella filling, eaten standing in the street. There's often a queue, but it moves fast. Closed on Sundays.
vp:luini: A panzerotto costs about €2.50–3 (from 2023 reviews, menu not seen): two and a drink come to under €10.
vd:marchesi: Milan's historic pâtisserie, with wood-panelled rooms and old-fashioned sweets: brioche, panettone, tartlets and coffee at the counter. It's expensive for breakfast at a table, but cheap at the counter. Hours and coordinates to be confirmed.
vp:marchesi: Brioche and coffee at the counter around €4–5 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:taveggia: A café-pâtisserie open since 1909 in San Babila, with displays of cakes, pastries and brioche. A good stop for breakfast or an afternoon snack, near the Duomo but away from the crush. Hours and coordinates to be confirmed.
vp:taveggia: Breakfast at the counter around €4–6 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:trattmil: A historic trattoria near the Biblioteca Ambrosiana, open since 1933: risotto alla milanese, ossobuco, cotoletta and panettone. Classic cooking, mixed reviews on how it's cooked. Closed on Sundays.
vp:trattmil: Upper-mid range: with a first and a main course you usually go over €30 per person (from guides, 2014 menu: risotto €11, cotoletta €19, more today).
vd:cucchi: A pâtisserie and café in Sant'Agostino, open since 1936: brioche and pastries, torta Paradiso, panettone in the colder months and coffee at the counter. Hours and coordinates to be confirmed; probably closed on Mondays.
vp:cucchi: Brioche and coffee at the counter around €3–5 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:premiata: A historic pizzeria on the Naviglio Grande: wood-fired Neapolitan pizza, Italian starters and tables in the street on warm evenings. In the evening there's always a queue: best to book. Hours and coordinates to be confirmed.
vp:premiata: A pizza usually costs €9–14: with a beer it comes to around €20 (from guides, menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:pave: The Porta Venezia bakery-pâtisserie, loved by people looking for flaky cornetti, baked cakes, bread and a good coffee. Eat at the little tables or standing up. Hours vary between sources: the website says 8am–7pm every day; other guides mention a closing day on Monday.
vp:pave: Cornetto and cappuccino around €5–7, a hot chocolate with a croissant comes to about €10 (from reviews, menu not seen).
vd:cotoletteria: A place in the Sarpi area whose one dish is the cotoletta alla milanese: classic, in a sandwich or with sauces. It's among the cheapest cotolette in Milan. Hours to be confirmed.
vp:cotoletteria: The classic cotoletta costs about €14 (from a 2026 guide), the variations €15–16. Hours to be confirmed.
cd:castellomusei: Michelangelo's Rondanini Pietà and rooms with frescoes and armour, inside the Castle.
cd:scienza: A real submarine and Leonardo's machines, in a former monastery.
cd:ambrosiana: The library with the Codex Atlanticus and Caravaggio's Basket of Fruit.
cd:galleriaditalia: 19th-century Lombard art in a palace on Piazza della Scala.
cd:poldi: A house museum with weapons, clocks and Pollaiolo's Portrait of a Woman.
cd:sansiro: Dressing rooms and stands of the Milan and Inter stadium, plus the museum.
cd:prada: A former distillery turned into a museum, with the Tower and Wes Anderson's Bar Luce.
cd:triennale: Italian design in a Rationalist building in Parco Sempione.
cd:mudec: The museum of cultures with temporary exhibitions, in a former factory.
cd:bagatti: A neo-Renaissance house full of furniture and weapons, in the fashion district.
cn:eustorgio: Basilica of Sant'Eustorgio and Portinari Chapel
cd:eustorgio: A Romanesque basilica with the Renaissance chapel frescoed by Foppa.
